items.title: Oil majors halt Strait of Hormuz shipments amid US-Iran strikes

featured_image.name: Oil: Iran partially closes Strait of Hormuz amid U.S. nuclear talks

items.description:
Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz ground to a near-halt on Saturday as oil majors and trading houses suspended crude oil, fuel, and liquefied natural gas shipments following joint US-Israeli military strikes on Iran. Tracking data showed tanker speeds dropping to near zero as shipowners pulled vessels from the waterway that carries roughly 20 percent of the world's seaborne oil trade.[1][2]

Several major oil companies and leading trading firms halted shipments through the strait as Iran declared the waterway closed to navigation, according to Reuters, citing four trading sources. "Our vessels will remain stationary for a number of days," a senior executive at a prominent trading firm said. The US Navy warned against navigating in the operational zone, which encompasses the entirety of the Gulf, the Gulf of Oman, the Arabian Sea, and the Strait of Hormuz, saying it could not guarantee the safety of commercial vessels.[2]

items.title: Trump announces 'major combat operations' in Iran

featured_image.name: Trump 'not thrilled' with Iran but undecided on attack

items.description:
President Donald Trump told reporters on Friday that he was "not happy" with the state of nuclear negotiations with Iran and warned that "sometimes you have to" use military force, remarks that proved to be a prelude to the launch of U.S. combat operations against Iran early Saturday.

Speaking outside the White House before departing for Texas, Trump said he had not yet made a final decision on strikes but expressed deep frustration with Tehran's negotiating posture. "I'm not happy with the fact that they're not willing to give us what we have to have," he said, according to Politico. "We're not thrilled with the way they're negotiating."[1][2]

Hours later, Trump announced on Truth Social that the United States had begun "major combat operations" in Iran, according to Reuters.[3]

items.title: Houthis to resume Red Sea attacks after U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: Houthi threaten to resume Red Sea attacks on shipping

items.description:
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels have decided to resume missile and drone attacks on Red Sea shipping routes and Israel in response to the joint U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran launched on February 28, two senior Houthi officials told the Associated Press. One official said the first attack could come as soon as "tonight," though no formal announcement had been issued by the Houthi leadership.[1][2][3]

The decision marks the collapse of a ceasefire between the Houthis and the United States that had been in place since May 2025, when the Trump administration and the group struck an Oman-brokered deal to halt mutual hostilities. Under that agreement, the Houthis ceased attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, while the U.S. ended its bombing campaign in Yemen. The Houthis had also stopped targeting Israel following an October 2025 ceasefire that reduced fighting in Gaza.[4][5][6][1]

items.title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at UAE in first direct attack

featured_image.name: Iran fires ballistic missiles at U.S. Al Dhafra Air Base in ...

items.description: The United Arab Emirates said on Saturday that its air defense systems intercepted multiple Iranian ballistic missiles targeting the country, though falling debris killed one civilian in Abu Dhabi and caused material damage in a residential area. The attack came as Iran launched retaliatory strikes across the Gulf following a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against targets inside Iran.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Russia may halt peace talks unless Ukraine cedes territory

featured_image.name: Russia and Ukraine stick to their demands ahead of planned ...

items.description:
Russian officials increasingly see little reason to continue U.S.-led peace negotiations with Ukraine unless Kyiv signals a willingness to give up territory as part of a settlement, Bloomberg News reported Saturday, raising the prospect of a collapse in diplomacy as the war enters its fifth year.[1][2]

Talks scheduled for next week will be decisive in whether the sides can move toward an agreement to end the conflict, two people close to the Kremlin told Bloomberg. Russia will likely walk away if Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy fails to make the concession, the people said. Reuters confirmed the report but said it could not independently verify the claims.[3][1]

items.title: Ohio State researchers turn moon dust into durable structures via 3D laser printing

featured_image.name: 3D-printed lunar base may be on the way

items.description:
Researchers at Ohio State University have demonstrated that laser-based 3D printing can transform simulated lunar soil into strong, heat-resistant structures, a advance that could one day allow astronauts to build habitats on the Moon using materials already found on its surface.

The study, published in the journal Acta Astronautica, offers a proof of concept for a technique that would eliminate the need to haul construction materials from Earth — a prospect that currently costs an estimated $1 million or more per kilogram, according to the researchers.[1]

items.title: Czech scientists detect lightning on Mars from orbit for the first time

featured_image.name: Listen to the crackle of Martian 'mini-lightning'

items.description: A team of Czech scientists has identified a lightning-generated radio signal in data from NASA's MAVEN spacecraft, providing the first orbital evidence of electrical discharge activity in the Martian atmosphere. The finding, published February 27 in the journal Science Advances, adds a new dimension to the growing body of evidence that Mars is an electrically active world.[1][2]

items.title: Trump launched Iran strikes despite intel doubting his missile threat claims

featured_image.name: President Trump addresses the nation after US strikes nuclear sites in Iran

items.description: Just days before the United States launched what President Donald Trump called "major combat operations" in Iran on Saturday, intelligence sources and weapons experts were pushing back on one of the administration's central justifications for military action: that Iran was close to building missiles capable of striking the American homeland.

items.title: Pentagon labels Anthropic a supply chain risk after AI safety standoff

featured_image.name: Hegseth declares Anthropic a "supply chain risk to national ...

items.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Friday designated AI company Anthropic a supply chain risk to national security, barring military contractors from doing business with the company after its CEO refused to lift safeguards on the use of its technology for mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons.

The move came shortly after President Trump ordered all federal agencies to "immediately cease" using Anthropic's technology. "We don't need it, we don't want it, and will not do business with them again!" Trump wrote on Truth Social, though he allowed a six-month phase-out period for the Defense Department and other agencies currently relying on the company's products.[1][2]

items.title: Chile bars Chinese hospital ship from treating locals amid US pressure

featured_image.name: Chile denies onboard care by Chinese medical ship as US ...

items.description:
Chile has refused to allow a Chinese hospital ship to provide medical services to local residents onboard, citing a lack of proper authorization, in a decision that underscores the growing geopolitical tug-of-war between Washington and Beijing across Latin America.

The medical vessel Silk Road Ark, currently on a voyage to roughly a dozen countries as part of China's "Mission Harmony 2025," arrived in waters off the Chilean port city of Valparaiso on Wednesday, according to Reuters. Chile's Ministry of Health said it had been reviewing a request submitted through the foreign ministry at the end of 2025 for the ship to offer medical care to locals, but ultimately declined. "We determined that it is not appropriate to authorize this health operation to function on the ship's facilities," the ministry said, pointing to a local health code that restricts such services to professionals accredited in the country.[1][2]

items.title: Ghana says 55 citizens killed fighting for Russia in Ukraine

featured_image.name: Ghana says at least 55 of its people killed after Russia 'lured' them to ...

items.description:
At least 55 Ghanaians have died fighting for Russia in Ukraine after being recruited through criminal trafficking networks, Ghana's Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said on Friday, marking one of the highest confirmed death tolls among African nations whose citizens have been drawn into the conflict.[1][2]

Ablakwa, who shared the figures on the social media platform X following high-level talks in Kyiv, said Ukrainian intelligence had documented 272 Ghanaians lured into the war since 2022, with two currently held as prisoners of war. "Ukrainian authorities revealed that from their credible intelligence gathering, they have documented 1,780 Africans from 36 countries who have been lured by criminal trafficking networks to join the war against Ukraine," Ablakwa said.[3][1]

items.title: Britain withdraws embassy staff from Iran amid US military buildup

featured_image.name: Starmer ‘supporting’ US-Iran talks after Trump threatens military action

items.description:
Britain withdrew its diplomatic staff from Iran and relocated embassy personnel inside Israel on Friday as a standoff with Washington over the use of the Diego Garcia military base deepened against a backdrop of faltering US-Iran nuclear negotiations and a massive American military buildup in the Middle East.

The White House is refusing to back the UK's agreement to hand sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius unless Prime Minister Keir Starmer allows the United States to use the jointly operated Diego Garcia base for potential strikes on Iran, according to Whitehall sources cited by GB News. Downing Street has so far resisted, with British officials arguing that permitting such an operation would violate international law.[1][2][3]

items.title: Fico says Ukraine has 'no interest' in restoring Druzhba oil pipeline after call with Zelenskyy

featured_image.name: Slovakia threatens to cut electricity to Ukraine over Russian oil spat

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico spoke by phone on Friday as a monthlong dispute over disrupted Russian oil supplies through the Druzhba pipeline showed no signs of resolution, with the standoff now blocking billions in EU financial aid to Kyiv and a new package of sanctions against Moscow.

Zelenskyy invited Fico to visit Ukraine to discuss "all issues" in person, according to a statement from the Ukrainian presidential office. Fico said he accepted the proposal for a meeting but would prefer it take place in an EU member state rather than in Ukraine. He offered a blunt assessment of the call: "I had the distinct impression that Ukraine has no interest in restoring oil transit through its territory."[1][2][3]

items.title: Meloni calls Trump tariffs a 'mistake,' proposes EU-US free-trade zone

featured_image.name: Italy's PM Meloni calls Trump's Greenland tariffs on Europe a mistake

items.description:
In an interview with Bloomberg published Friday, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called for the European Union to form a free-trade zone with the United States, an ambitious proposal aimed at resolving the transatlantic tariff standoff that has rattled markets and stalled trade policy on both sides of the Atlantic.[1][2]

Meloni described President Donald Trump's tariffs as a "mistake" and urged the EU to move forward with adopting the trade agreement it struck with Washington last summer, known as the Turnberry deal, according to Bloomberg. The deal, reached at Trump's Scottish golf resort in July 2025, set a 15% ceiling on tariffs for most EU exports to the United States in exchange for the EU eliminating import duties on all US industrial goods.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Taliban signal willingness to talk after Pakistan launches airstrikes

featured_image.name: Pakistan says ‘patience has run out' as it bombs Taliban across Afghanistan

items.description:
Afghanistan's Taliban government said Friday it was open to negotiations with Pakistan, even as the two nations exchanged their most serious cross-border attacks in years. The diplomatic overture came hours after Pakistan launched airstrikes on Kabul, Kandahar, and Paktia province, with its defense minister declaring that the countries are now in a state of "open war."[1][2][3]

The conflicting signals — a willingness to talk paired with escalating military operations — underscore the volatile and rapidly shifting dynamics between the once-allied neighbors, whose relationship has deteriorated sharply over Pakistan's accusations that the Taliban harbors militant groups responsible for attacks inside Pakistani territory.

items.title: Trump warns of military force against Iran as nuclear talks stall

featured_image.name: Trump's claim on Iranian missile development said ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Friday expressed frustration with the progress of nuclear negotiations with Iran and warned that military force remains on the table, telling reporters, "Don't want to, but sometimes you have to," when asked whether he would order strikes against the Islamic Republic.[1][2]

Speaking to reporters before departing the White House for a trip to Texas, Trump said he was "not happy" with Iran's posture in the talks and reiterated his core demand. "I'm not happy with the fact that they're not willing to give us what we have to have. I'm not thrilled with that," he said, adding: "Iran cannot have nuclear weapons".[3][4]

items.title: IAEA says Iran stored near-weapons-grade uranium underground

featured_image.name: IAEA chief says Iran could be enriching uranium within ...

items.description:
Some of Iran's most highly enriched uranium was stored in an underground tunnel complex at its nuclear site in Isfahan prior to last year's U.S. strikes, the International Atomic Energy Agency said in a confidential report circulated to member states on Friday, marking the first time the U.N. nuclear watchdog has specified where uranium enriched to up to 60% purity has been kept.[1][2]

The disclosure adds a new dimension to the standoff over Tehran's nuclear program, arriving as the United States and Iran pursue fragile diplomatic negotiations and Washington maintains a large military buildup across the Middle East.

items.title: Green Party wins first-ever UK by-election, pushing Labour to third

featured_image.name: UK Greens trounce far right in key election as Labour fall to ...

items.description: Hannah Spencer, a 34-year-old plumber and local councillor, has won the Gorton and Denton by-election in Greater Manchester, delivering a result that marks the first time in the Green Party's history that it has won a UK parliamentary by-election. The victory, declared in the early hours of Friday morning, saw Spencer capture 14,980 votes — roughly 40.7% of the total — overturning a Labour majority of more than 13,000 from the 2024 general election. The result pushes Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party into third place in a seat the party had held for nearly a century.[1][2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: OpenAI raises record $110B from Amazon, Nvidia, SoftBank

featured_image.name: OpenAI said to be finalizing $100 billion funding round

items.description:
OpenAI announced on Friday a $110 billion funding round at a $730 billion pre-money valuation, the largest private financing deal ever recorded. The round includes $50 billion from Amazon, $30 billion from Nvidia, and $30 billion from SoftBank, with additional financial investors expected to join as the round progresses.[1]

The deal cements a sweeping strategic partnership between OpenAI and Amazon and deepens the AI company's ties to its largest chip supplier, Nvidia, while more than doubling the $40 billion OpenAI raised in March 2025 in what was then the biggest private tech fundraise on record.[2]

items.title: Chinese scientists set world records for kesterite, polymer solar cells

featured_image.name: Kesterite solar cells get ready to shine

items.description:
Researchers in China have announced back-to-back breakthroughs in solar cell technology, setting world records for both kesterite and polymer photovoltaic devices in findings published this week.

The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) reported that its Qingdao Institute of Bioenergy and Bioprocess Technology fabricated a kesterite solar cell achieving a power conversion efficiency of 15.45%, with a certified efficiency of 15.04%, according to pv magazine. Separately, a team at Wuhan University of Technology unveiled a polymer solar cell reaching 19.1% efficiency while retaining 97% of its performance after 2,000 hours of operation in air.[1][2]
